meta.description: Catalogue of Geometry Dash editor objects: official name, engine behaviour, collision, and how each one is used.
sources: Web Dashers allObjects.js (engine behaviour: type, grid size, sprite, colour rules)

roles.unknown: not present in the engine object list

legend_engine_types.soliddeco: Looks like a solid block but has NO collision.

0.name: object 0
0.how_it_works: The player collides with it. Landing on its top surface is safe; touching its side or underside kills. These are platforms, floors, walls, ceilings and stairs. A continuous row at ground level is a WALL, not a floor - the engine already supplies the ground.

1.name: Black Gradient Square
1.summary: The classic solid block. Used for floating platforms and scenery.
1.how_it_works: Build floors and platforms from these, but let the engine's own ground carry the player along the bottom of the level.

tested.label: solid block floating 2 blocks up
tested.confidence: LOW - collision x-frame unconfirmed; treat as unverified

2.name: Grid Patterned Top Square

tested.label: grid-topped block at ground level
tested.confidence: LOW - collision x-frame unconfirmed; treat as unverified

8.name: Black Gradient Spike
8.summary: The classic ground spike. One block wide, kills on contact.
8.how_it_works: The workhorse hazard. A single spike is cleared by one cube jump; two or three in a row need an earlier jump.

tested.label: ground spike
tested.confidence: LOW - collision x-frame unconfirmed; treat as unverified

9.name: pit_01_001.png

10.name: Blue Gravity Portal

10.how_it_works: Used to return to normal gravity after a ceiling section.

45.name: Orange Mirror Portal

661.name: Outline Small Square
661.how_it_works: The player collides with it. Landing on its top surface is safe; touching its side or underside kills. These are platforms, floors, walls, ceilings and stairs. A continuous row at ground level is a WALL, not a floor - the engine already supplies the ground.

747.name: Linked Teleport Portals
747.how_it_works: Triggers when the player's body overlaps it, changing mode, gravity, size, mirroring or dual state.
